newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall to close below 2,300.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall to close below 2,300.

text.p: French stocks closed sharply lower on Thursday after the bourse reversed its early gains to track a correction in the bond markets and a wobbly start in trading on Wall Street, brokers said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 16.15 points, or 0.7 percent, at 2,292.50, while the CAC-40 December futures contract fell 15.5 points to 2,294.50. Volume was 5.85 billion francs, a substantial turnover but below recent levels.
Analysts say the market was due for a pause after a sharp recent rise that brought the CAC close to its all-time record of 2,360.98 points, set in February 1994.

Brokers said the market turned lower after the central banks of France and Germany failed to deliver anticipated interest rate cuts on Thursday. With the dollar weaker, all the trends that had driven the bourse higher were temporarily stalled.
Brokers said investors, foreigners in particular, were baffled and discouraged by the suspension announced on Wednesday of the privatisation of electronics group Thomson.

* Alcatel Alsthom, whose bid had been rejected by the government in October but was favoured by the privatisation commission in its report, extended the previous day's loss, losing a further three francs to close at 457.
* Lagardere, hammered on Wednesday when the government suspended the plan to sell Thomson to Lagardere, staged a weak rebound, adding one franc to 146.
* Oil majors Elf-Aquitaine and Total fell 3.06 percent and 1.86 percent, respectively, after Merrill Lynch downgraded its short-term recommendations on the stocks.

* PSA Peugeot Citroen shares fell 2.51 percent to close at 622 francs. Peugeot Automobiles said it was having difficulties in China and was considering withdrawing from one of its two production sites. On the plus side, British car sales for November showed a big rise in the group's market share.
Early on Thursday, a block of shares representing 2.6 percent of the group's capital was placed by Michelin at 614 francs per share, leaving the tyremaker with 3.5 percent of PSA Peugeot Citroen.

* Luxury goods group LVMH, a big recent gainer helped by its blue-chip status and the dollar's gains, fell 2.21 percent to 1,325 francs in profit-taking. Holding company Dior similarly fell 3.87 percent to 745.
* Bouygues adds 2.68 percent in technical rebound.
* Schneider active with two block trades of 200,000 and 71,000 shares. The stock closed down 1.06 percent.
